description: Competency questions defining the scope of the wound ontology. Organised by clinical question. Questions the ontology must answer (in_scope) or explicitly cannot answer (out_of_scope).

clinical_themes.theme: What is a wound? What is not a wound?

in_scope.question: Is a diabetic wound a type of wound?
in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-16: was 'Diabetic Foot Ulcer is_a Chronic Wound'. No wound class is chronic by definition (every wound starts acute), so nothing may be asserted under Chronic wound; and WONT models the diabetic wound, not the foot site. The subsumption asked for is the one WONT holds.

in_scope.question: Is a pressure ulcer a type of wound?
in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-16: was 'is_a Chronic Wound' -- same reason as CQ001. Expected to FAIL until WONT mints its own pressure ulcer class (the label currently resolves to HP_0012399, a phenotype); see WONT_TODO.

in_scope.question: Is a surgical site infection a type of wound complication?
in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-17: a surgical site infection is a disease, not a process, so it cannot be a subclass of 'wound complication process'. WONT now has the material class 'Wound complication' (MILD_120051 branch) and files SSI under it.

in_scope.question: Is a burn injury a type of traumatic wound?
Is a venous leg ulcer a venous insufficiency wound?
in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-16: was 'Venous Leg Ulcer is_a Chronic Wound' -- same reason as CQ001. The venous axis is what WONT asserts of this class (label 'Wound co-located with impaired venous backflow' until 2026-09-17).

out_of_scope.question: Is a bone fracture a wound?
out_of_scope.reason: Fracture is an orthopaedic injury — not a soft-tissue wound concept in this ontology.

out_of_scope.question: Is a myocardial infarction a wound?
out_of_scope.reason: Organ infarction is not within the wound care domain.

out_of_scope.question: Is necrotizing fasciitis a type of wound?
out_of_scope.reason: Premise rejected 2026-09-17 (curator): necrotizing fasciitis is an infection that occurs without any wound being present at the time of infection, so it is not a type of wound.

out_of_scope.question: Is an abscess a type of wound?
out_of_scope.reason: Premise rejected 2026-09-17 (curator): an abscess is an infection of a hair follicle under intact skin; the skin is intact, so it is not a wound.

out_of_scope.question: Is a laceration a type of acute wound?
out_of_scope.reason: Premise rejected 2026-09-17 (curator): a laceration is not acute by definition - it is chronic if it does not heal. No wound class is acute or chronic by definition (ruling of 2026-09-16). WONT holds Laceration ⊑ Traumatic wound.

in_scope.question: What causes a pressure injury?
in_scope.rewrite: 'caused_by' -> 'co_located_with' (2026-09) -> 'complication_of' (2026-09-17). MILD commitment 4 refuses aetiology between disorders; the assertable question is whether the subject is the output of a development process that has a wound causing process of the object's disease course as part (MILD_120053). Co-location only said a diagnostic classification files the two under one disease.

out_of_scope.question: What contaminates a wound with bacteria?
out_of_scope.reason: Premise rejected 2026-09-17 (curator): bacterial colonization is a process on the IWII continuum, not a disease course, and a wound infection process is not the output of it. Colonized and infected are grades of the same scale in WONT.

out_of_scope.question: What causes biofilm formation in a wound?
out_of_scope.reason: Premise rejected 2026-09-17 (curator): a wound biofilm is not the output of a bacterial colonization process in the sense of a complication; see CQ042.

out_of_scope.question: What pathogen causes necrotizing fasciitis?
out_of_scope.reason: Retired 2026-09-17 (curator): necrotizing fasciitis is an infection, not a wound (CQ005); which pathogen causes it is a question about a disease, outside WONT's scope.

in_scope.question: Is negative pressure wound therapy a method of wound treatment?
in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-17: is_treatment_for is not needed (curator). An agent - dressing, drug, device - participates in a treatment process, and the wound participates in every wound treatment process; that is what the ontology asserts. The condition named before was in any case not what the intervention treats by definition. 'Chronic wound' dropped: no wound is chronic by definition and NPWT is not confined to them.

in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-17: wound healing phases are a classification scheme (WONT_0000561, a wound classification grade) whose grades are individuals, as every grade in WONT is. A grade is an information entity: it is not part_of the healing process and a process is not a kind of it. The scheme is about wound healing and each grade is about the processes it labels, which is what the question can ask.

clinical_themes.theme: What complications can follow a wound?

in_scope.question: Is wound infection a type of wound complication?
Is wound dehiscence a type of wound complication?
in_scope.note: REVERTED a label fix. Mapping 'Wound Complication' to 'wound complication process' made this triple a category error: Wound dehiscence is a MILD_120022 pathological disorder, not a process, so it can never be a subclass of a process. The ontology's material counterpart is 'material complication disease entity' - but choosing it is a modelling decision, not a label fix, so it is left for review.
in_scope.rewrite: Rewritten 2026-09-17: 'Wound complication' (WONT_0000557) is a material complication disease entity (MILD_120051) and wound dehiscence is a pathological disorder; a disorder is not a disease. The disorder-level class 'Wound complication disorder' (WONT_0000588, ⊑ MILD_120022) is what dehiscence is a kind of; the disease-level class has it as part.

Co-location only said a diagnostic classification files the two under one disease.

out_of_scope.question: Is sepsis a type of wound complication?
out_of_scope.reason: Premise rejected 2026-09-17 (curator): sepsis is not a wound complication by definition; it can be one, which is not a class-level statement.

out_of_scope.question: What causes wound dehiscence?
out_of_scope.reason: Premise rejected 2026-09-17 (curator): wound dehiscence is not a wound development, and it is not the output of a wound infection process by definition. The dehiscence process is a disorder development process (WONT_0000433).

out_of_scope.question: Is osteomyelitis a complication of an open wound?
out_of_scope.reason: Premise rejected 2026-09-17 (curator): osteomyelitis is not a wound complication by definition; it can be one, which is not a class-level statement (as CQ071, sepsis).
